question: There are 5 jobs labeled Job 0 to Job 4, each requiring processing on 4 machines labeled Machine 0 to Machine 3. Each job has a specific processing time on each machine: Job 0 takes 5 hours on Machine 0, 9 hours on Machine 1, 7 hours on Machine 2, and 7 hours on Machine 3; Job 1 takes 10 hours on Machine 0, 8 hours on Machine 1, 8 hours on Machine 2, and 9 hours on Machine 3; Job 2 takes 6 hours on Machine 0, 8 hours on Machine 1, 9 hours on Machine 2, and 7 hours on Machine 3; Job 3 takes 7 hours on Machine 0, 7 hours on Machine 1, 8 hours on Machine 2, and 8 hours on Machine 3; Job 4 takes 9 hours on Machine 0, 5 hours on Machine 1, 5 hours on Machine 2, and 9 hours on Machine 3. Each job must be assigned to exactly one position in the schedule, and each position must be assigned exactly one job. A job cannot start on a machine until it has completed processing on the previous machine in the sequence. Additionally, a job in a later position in the schedule cannot start on a machine until the job in the previous position has completed processing on that machine. The objective is to minimize the total completion time, which includes the start time of the last job on the last machine (Machine 3) and the processing time of the last job on Machine 3. The start times for each job on each machine must be non-negative, and all constraints must be satisfied to avoid delays and resource conflicts.

DATA = {
    # "There are 5 jobs labeled Job 0 to Job 4"
    "num_jobs": 5,
    # "each requiring processing on 4 machines labeled Machine 0 to Machine 3"
    "num_machines": 4,
    # Processing times p[job][machine]
    # "Job 0 takes 5 hours on Machine 0, 9 hours on Machine 1, 7 hours on Machine 2, and 7 hours on Machine 3"
    "proc_time": {
        0: {0: 5, 1: 9, 2: 7, 3: 7},
        # "Job 1 takes 10 hours on Machine 0, 8 hours on Machine 1, 8 hours on Machine 2, and 9 hours on Machine 3"
        1: {0: 10, 1: 8, 2: 8, 3: 9},
        # "Job 2 takes 6 hours on Machine 0, 8 hours on Machine 1, 9 hours on Machine 2, and 7 hours on Machine 3"
        2: {0: 6, 1: 8, 2: 9, 3: 7},
        # "Job 3 takes 7 hours on Machine 0, 7 hours on Machine 1, 8 hours on Machine 2, and 8 hours on Machine 3"
        3: {0: 7, 1: 7, 2: 8, 3: 8},
        # "Job 4 takes 9 hours on Machine 0, 5 hours on Machine 1, 5 hours on Machine 2, and 9 hours on Machine 3"
        4: {0: 9, 1: 5, 2: 5, 3: 9},
    },
    # Big-M: safe upper bound on any start/finish time
    "bigM": 5 * 10 * 4,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    nJ = d["num_jobs"]
    nM = d["num_machines"]
    p = d["proc_time"]
    M = d["bigM"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # Sets
    model.J = pyo.RangeSet(0, nJ - 1)          # jobs
    model.M = pyo.RangeSet(0, nM - 1)          # machines
    model.P = pyo.RangeSet(0, nJ - 1)          # positions
    model.Mprev = pyo.RangeSet(0, nM - 2)      # machines with a successor
    model.Pprev = pyo.RangeSet(1, nJ - 1)      # positions with a predecessor

    # Variables
    # x[j,p] = 1 if job j is assigned to position p
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.J, model.P, within=pyo.Binary)

    # s[j,m] = start time of job j on machine m (non-negative)
    model.s = pyo.Var(model.J, model.M, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Cmax = total completion time (makespan)
    model.Cmax = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Assignment constraints
    def job_once_rule(m, j):
        return sum(m.x[j, pp] for pp in m.P) == 1
    model.job_once = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=job_once_rule)

    def pos_once_rule(m, pp):
        return sum(m.x[j, pp] for j in m.J) == 1
    model.pos_once = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=pos_once_rule)

    # Machine precedence within a job: s[j,m+1] >= s[j,m] + p[j,m]
    def within_job_rule(m, j, mm):
        return m.s[j, mm + 1] >= m.s[j, mm] + p[j][mm]
    model.within_job = pyo.Constraint(model.J, model.Mprev, rule=within_job_rule)

    # Position precedence on each machine: the job at position p starts after the
    # job at position p-1 finishes on the same machine.
    # Linearised with big-M and assignment variables.
    def pos_prec_rule(m, mm, pp, j, k):
        return m.s[j, mm] >= m.s[k, mm] + p[k][mm] - M * (
            2 - m.x[j, pp] - m.x[k, pp - 1]
        )
    model.pos_prec = pyo.Constraint(
        model.M, model.Pprev, model.J, model.J, rule=pos_prec_rule
    )

    # Makespan: Cmax >= s[j, last_machine] + p[j][last_machine] for every job
    last_m = nM - 1
    def makespan_rule(m, j):
        return m.Cmax >= m.s[j, last_m] + p[j][last_m]
    model.makespan = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=makespan_rule)

    # Objective: minimize total completion time (makespan)
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.Cmax, sense=pyo.minimize)

    return model

import pyomo.environ as pyo

# =============================================================================
# PROBLEM: 5 jobs (0..4) on 4 machines (0..3), flow-shop style with a
# permutation sequence.  Each job is assigned to exactly one position in the
# schedule and each position holds exactly one job.  A job visits machines
# 0,1,2,3 in order (precedence within a job).  A job in a later position
# cannot start on a machine until the job in the previous position has
# finished that machine (no overlap on a machine).  Minimise the makespan.
#
# DECISION VARIABLES
#   x[j, p]  : Binary, 1 if job j occupies schedule position p.        (assign)
#   s[j, m]  : NonNegativeReal, start time of job j on machine m.      (timing)
#   Cmax     : NonNegativeReal, makespan (completion of last job on M3).(objective)
#
# OBJECTIVE (words): minimise Cmax, the total completion time = start time of
#   the last job on the last machine plus its processing time on that machine.
#
# CONSTRAINTS (numbered, with source sentence)
#   (1) Each job assigned to exactly one position.        "Each job must be
#       assigned to exactly one position in the schedule"
#   (2) Each position assigned exactly one job.           "each position must
#       be assigned exactly one job"
#   (3) Precedence within a job: s[j,m+1] >= s[j,m] + p[j,m].  "A job cannot
#       start on a machine until it has completed processing on the previous
#       machine in the sequence"
#   (4) Machine non-overlap between consecutive positions: for the job in
#       position p and the job in position p+1, the later one starts on
#       machine m only after the earlier one finishes.  "a job in a later
#       position in the schedule cannot start on a machine until the job in
#       the previous position has completed processing on that machine"
#   (5) Makespan definition: Cmax >= s[j,last] + p[j,last] for the job in the
#       last position.  "includes the start time of the last job on the last
#       machine (Machine 3) and the processing time of the last job on
#       Machine 3"
#   (6) Non-negativity of start times.  "start times ... must be non-negative"
# =============================================================================

DATA = {
    "num_jobs": 5,
    "num_machines": 4,
    # processing_time[j][m] = time of job j on machine m
    "processing_time": [
        [5, 9, 7, 7],   # Job 0
        [10, 8, 8, 9],  # Job 1
        [6, 8, 9, 7],   # Job 2
        [7, 7, 8, 8],   # Job 3
        [9, 5, 5, 9],   # Job 4
    ],
    # big-M: an upper bound on any start time / makespan
    "big_M": 1000,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    n_jobs = d["num_jobs"]
    n_mach = d["num_machines"]
    p = d["processing_time"]
    M = d["big_M"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # ---- Sets -------------------------------------------------------------
    model.JOBS = pyo.RangeSet(0, n_jobs - 1)
    model.MACHINES = pyo.RangeSet(0, n_mach - 1)
    model.POSITIONS = pyo.RangeSet(0, n_jobs - 1)
    # machines excluding the last one (for precedence within a job)
    model.MACHINES_PREV = pyo.RangeSet(0, n_mach - 2)

    # ---- Variables --------------------------------------------------------
    # x[j, p] = 1 if job j is placed in schedule position p
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.JOBS, model.POSITIONS,
                      domain=pyo.Binary)

    # s[j, m] = start time of job j on machine m
    model.s = pyo.Var(model.JOBS, model.MACHINES,
                      domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # makespan
    model.Cmax = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # ---- Objective --------------------------------------------------------
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.Cmax, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # ---- Constraint (1): each job in exactly one position ----------------
    def job_assignment_rule(m, j):
        return sum(m.x[j, pos] for pos in m.POSITIONS) == 1
    model.job_assignment = pyo.Constraint(model.JOBS,
                                          rule=job_assignment_rule)

    # ---- Constraint (2): each position holds exactly one job -------------
    def position_assignment_rule(m, pos):
        return sum(m.x[j, pos] for j in m.JOBS) == 1
    model.position_assignment = pyo.Constraint(model.POSITIONS,
                                               rule=position_assignment_rule)

    # ---- Constraint (3): precedence within a job -------------------------
    def job_precedence_rule(m, j, mm):
        return m.s[j, mm + 1] >= m.s[j, mm] + p[j][mm]
    model.job_precedence = pyo.Constraint(model.JOBS, model.MACHINES_PREV,
                                          rule=job_precedence_rule)

    # ---- Constraint (4): machine non-overlap between consecutive positions
    # For each machine mm and each consecutive position pair (pos, pos+1),
    # the job in position pos+1 must start after the job in position pos
    # finishes on machine mm.
    #   s[j2, mm] >= s[j1, mm] + p[j1][mm] - M*(2 - x[j1,pos] - x[j2,pos+1])
    # The big-M term deactivates the constraint unless j1 is in pos and j2 is
    # in pos+1.
    model.POS_PAIRS = pyo.RangeSet(0, n_jobs - 2)

    def machine_order_rule(m, mm, pos, j1, j2):
        return (m.s[j2, mm]
                >= m.s[j1, mm] + p[j1][mm]
                - M * (2 - m.x[j1, pos] - m.x[j2, pos + 1]))
    model.machine_order = pyo.Constraint(
        model.MACHINES, model.POS_PAIRS, model.JOBS, model.JOBS,
        rule=machine_order_rule)

    # ---- Constraint (5): makespan definition -----------------------------
    # Cmax >= s[j, last] + p[j][last] for the job j in the last position.
    last_machine = n_mach - 1
    last_position = n_jobs - 1

    def makespan_rule(m, j):
        return (m.Cmax
                >= m.s[j, last_machine] + p[j][last_machine]
                - M * (1 - m.x[j, last_position]))
    model.makespan_def = pyo.Constraint(model.JOBS, rule=makespan_rule)

    # ---- Constraint (6): non-negativity is enforced by variable domain ---

    return model

        return m.C >= m.s[j, last_m] + d["proc"][(j, last_m)]

    nm = d["num_machines"]

    # t[k,m] = start time of the job at position k on machine m
    model.t = pyo.Var(model.P, model.M,
                      domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, B))

    # makespan / total completion time
    model.Cmax = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, B))

    # ---- Objective ----
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.Cmax, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # ---- Assignment: each job to exactly one position ----
    def job_once_rule(m, j):
        return sum(m.x[j, k] for k in m.P) == 1
    model.job_assigned = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=job_once_rule)

    # ---- Assignment: each position gets exactly one job ----
    def pos_once_rule(m, k):
        return sum(m.x[j, k] for j in m.J) == 1
    model.pos_filled = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=pos_once_rule)

    # ---- Precedence within a job: machine m+1 after machine m done ----
    # The job at position k on machine (m+1) starts at least processing time
    # on machine m after its machine-m start:
    #   t[k,m+1] >= t[k,m] + sum_j p[j,m] * x[j,k]
    def prec_machine_rule(m, k, mch):
        if mch == d["machines"][-1]:
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        proc_at_pos = sum(d["process"][j][mch] * m.x[j, k] for j in m.J)
        return m.t[k, mch + 1] >= m.t[k, mch] + proc_at_pos
    model.precedence_within_job = pyo.Constraint(
        model.P, model.M, rule=prec_machine_rule)

    # ---- Position ordering: consecutive positions on same machine ----
    # job at position k starts machine m after job at position k-1 finishes m:
    #   t[k,m] >= t[k-1,m] + sum_j p[j,m] * x[j,k-1]
    def pos_order_rule(m, k, mch):
        if k == d["positions"][0]:
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        proc_prev = sum(d["process"][j][mch] * m.x[j, k - 1] for j in m.J)
        return m.t[k, mch] >= m.t[k - 1, mch] + proc_prev
    model.pos_ordering = pyo.Constraint(
        model.P, model.M, rule=pos_order_rule)

    # ---- Makespan: completion of last machine for the last position ----
    # Cmax >= t[last_pos, last_machine] + processing of that job on last machine
    last_k = d["positions"][-1]
    last_m = d["machines"][-1]

    def makespan_rule(m):
        proc_last = sum(d["process"][j][last_m] * m.x[j, last_k] for j in m.J)
        return m.Cmax >= m.t[last_k, last_m] + proc_last
    model.makespan_def = pyo.Constraint(rule=makespan_rule)

    return model
